notes.meaning: David cries out to God, asking Him to listen and bring relief from his troubles. He looks back at how God made room for him when he was squeezed into tight corners before. Because God has been faithful in the past, David boldly asks for mercy once again. Remembering how God helped us yesterday gives us courage to pray today.

differ.view: Some Baptists emphasize that God is called the God of righteousness because He makes the believer righteous by crediting Christ's righteousness to them.
Many in this tradition hold that the title means God is the defender of David's innocent cause against the false charges of his enemies.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars translate the phrase as 'God who vindicates me' and see David describing his deliverance as so certain that it is spoken of as already accomplished.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine reads the prayer in the past tense, explaining that God has already brought the soul out of the narrow grip of sorrow into the open space of spiritual joy.

notes.meaning: David speaks directly to powerful leaders who are dragging his royal honor through the dirt. He asks them how long they will chase after empty schemes and spread slanderous lies. Their rebellion is a hopeless effort that can never succeed against the ruler God chose. Sin always promises what it cannot deliver.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some interpreters suggest that 'vanity' and 'lies' refer to false gods, though most take the words as describing sinful plots against the king.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explains this as a call for all people to turn away from low, passing worldly pleasures and seek the only truth that brings lasting happiness.

notes.meaning: David warns his foes that the Lord sets apart those who love Him for His own special purpose. Because God has chosen David and protects him, He will surely hear when David calls out for help. Anyone who fights against God's servant is fighting against God Himself. God always listens closely to the prayers of those who belong to Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interprets the godly one as Christ, whom God set apart and exalted by raising Him from the dead to sit at His right hand.

notes.meaning: David commands his opponents to stop their rebellion and avoid falling deeper into sin. He tells them to go to bed, quietly search their own hearts, and let their anger cool down in the stillness of the night. Quiet self-examination keeps raw emotions from turning into wicked actions.

differ.view: Methodist writers such as John Wesley read this as 'Stand in awe,' urging rebels to fear God's judgment and drop their opposition to His authority.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine teaches that this means either checking our anger before we act on it, or becoming angry at our own past sins so that we turn away from them.

notes.meaning: David tells the people to come to God with genuine worship and put their full trust in Him. Outward rituals mean nothing unless they are offered with a pure heart and true obedience. God welcomes our service only when our faith rests entirely on Him.

differ.view: The Geneva notes explain these sacrifices as living righteously and serving God purely, rather than depending on outward temple ceremonies.
Adam Clarke holds that this refers to actual animal offerings required by the Law, which had to be brought with honest faith and true repentance to be accepted.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine sees these sacrifices as the offering of a broken spirit and a reformed life, which God values far above animal gifts.

notes.meaning: Many people look around in doubt, asking where they can find good things and earthly prosperity. David answers that longing with a prayer for the light of God's face, asking for God's loving presence and favor. Real happiness is not found in possessions, but in knowing God is smiling on us.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching interprets the light of God's face as the imprint of divine truth on human reason, which guides the conscience to choose good over evil.

notes.meaning: God gives David a deep, inner gladness that worldly wealth could never provide. This spiritual joy is far greater than the celebration people have during a huge harvest of grain and wine. When God fills the soul with His grace, a believer has plenty even when life is hard.

David finishes his evening prayer by lying down to sleep in complete calm and peace. He does not need armed guards or perfect surroundings, because the Lord alone keeps him safe from harm. We can rest without fear when we leave ourselves in God's hands.
